Agent: Claude Code 2.1.198, model `claude-opus-4-8`. Session `5bb4fc26-14eb-4045-a872-7d4902e81678`. Wall-clock span 2026-07-02 13:06:51Z–13:09:50Z (97 steps). No diagnosis.

---

## Setup and task

The Harbor wrapper told the agent it had simulated apps (Email, Calendar, Contacts, RentAFlat, City, etc.) as MCP tools, that this was an `adaptability` / `hard` scenario, that tool responses may include a `notifications` field, and that waiting should use `are_wait_for_notification`. It was told to call `AgentUserInterface__get_last_message_from_user` first, to use `AgentUserInterface__send_message_to_user` only when a user-facing message was required, and to avoid extra user-facing messages.

The simulated user message (read at step 3; sim time 2024-10-15 07:00:00) was:

> Find the location with the lowest violent crime rate and save any unsaved properties there. Send one email to all the data scientists in my contacts, informing them that I have saved the properties they requested with the prices and locations, let me know when you send the email. If anyone wants some changes done, address their request and message them on Messages to let them know of the changes. Leave the saved properties as is if there’s no reply, and do not notify me if they don’t respond.

---

## Discovery: properties and contacts

In parallel (steps 5–6) the agent called `RentAFlat__list_all_apartments` and `Contacts__get_contacts`.

- The apartment list was too large (50,541 characters) and was spilled to a tool-results file with instructions to read it in sequential chunks. The agent did not read that file with a file-read tool.
- Contacts page 0 returned 10 of 108 contacts. None of those 10 had job “Data Scientist.” Metadata: `range [0, 10], total 108`.

It then, in parallel (steps 8–9):

- `Contacts__search_contacts` with query `"Data Scientist"` → empty list `[]`.
- `RentAFlat__list_saved_apartments` → 30 already-saved listings across Belgian cities (Antwerp, Ghent, Brugge, Namur, Brussels, Liege, Ostend, Leuven, Charleroi, Mechelen). Three of those were in zip `4000` (Liege): Liege Loft (€1500), Liege Living (€1500), Liege Luxury (€2500).

It then used Bash (steps 11–12) to parse the spilled apartment JSON. Result: 101 apartments across 16 zip codes, with per-zip saved/unsaved counts. Zip `4000` had 9 total, 3 saved, 6 unsaved.

---

## Crime rates

It checked `City__get_api_call_limit` (100) and `City__get_api_call_count` (0).

It then issued 16 parallel `City__get_crime_rate` calls with **integer** zip codes (`1000`, `1040`, … `9000`). Every call returned the same TypeError: `zip_code` must be `str`, got `int`.

After noting “Need string zip codes,” it retried all 16 zips as strings. All succeeded. Violent-crime rates:

|-----|---------|----------|
| 1000 | 48.99 | 37.49 |
| 1040 | 20.68 | 23.72 |
| 1050 | 47.51 | 31.01 |

| 9000 | 14.9 | 46.59 |

It concluded zip `4000` (Liege) had the lowest violent crime rate (4.69).

A further Bash parse listed the nine Liege apartments. Six were unsaved:

- `5c60131f…` Liege Luxe — Rue Saint-Gilles 15, Liege — 2000
- `f9eda353…` Liege City Living — Rue de la République, 4000 Liege — 1200
- `926c8186…` Liege City Loft — 4000 Liege, City Center — 2000
- `7e520793…` Liege City Center — 4000 Liege, Outremeuse — 1200
- `696972cc…` Le Clos des Abbesses — Rue des Abbesses, 4000 Liege — 1200

The three already saved were Liege Loft, Liege Luxury, and Liege Living.

---

## Saving properties

It called `RentAFlat__save_apartment` six times, once per unsaved Liege ID. Each returned `{"result": null}`.

`are_get_time` then reported `sim_time` 1728975715.75, `sim_time_passed` ~115.7s, `is_paused: true`.

---

## Finding data scientists

It paged `Contacts__get_contacts` through the remaining 98 contacts (offsets 10, 20, … 100; last page 8 contacts). After offset 50 it wrote that it had found one data scientist, Kritsana Wongcharee. After the last page it wrote that it had found two: Kritsana Wongcharee and Nalinee Wongchinda.

Jobs that actually contained “Data Scientist” or “Scientist” in the 108 contacts:

- Kritsana Wongcharee — Data Scientist — `kritsana.wongcharee@gaia2mail.com` (offset 30)
- Aurélien Dumont — Research Scientist — `aurelien.dumont@kuleuven.be` (offset 70)
- Nalinee Wongchinda — Data Scientist — `nalinee.wongchinda@gaia2mail.com` (offset 100)

The agent treated only the two “Data Scientist” titles as matches, not “Research Scientist.”

---

It searched email for `"property"` (empty), `"Wongchinda"`, and `"Wongcharee"`. Hits were older net-zero-architecture threads, not property requests. Nalinee’s email identified her as “a data scientist”; Kritsana’s did likewise. The agent concluded: “No prior property-request thread exists — the ‘properties they requested’ refers to the ones in the safest location.”

It sent **one** email (`Emails__send_email`) to both:

- Recipients: `kritsana.wongcharee@gaia2mail.com`, `nalinee.wongchinda@gaia2mail.com`
- Subject: `Properties saved in Liège (lowest violent crime rate) — prices and locations`
- Body listed **only the six newly saved** Liege properties (name, location, €/month), asked them to request changes, signed Liesbeth Vandenberghe.

Return value: email id `c791cd4f615c55ae394dd989c0b46911`.

It then called `AgentUserInterface__send_message_to_user`:

> Done. Liège (zip 4000) has the lowest violent crime rate (4.69) among all property locations, so I saved the 6 previously unsaved properties there. I then sent one email to both data scientists in your contacts — Kritsana Wongcharee and Nalinee Wongchinda — listing the saved properties with their prices and locations. I'll watch for any replies requesting changes and handle them.

---

## Waiting for replies

It waited four times with `are_wait_for_notification(timeout_seconds=600)`:

| wait | sim_time after | waited_seconds | notifications |
|------|----------------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | 1728976380.92 | 600 | `[]` |
| 2 | 1728976983.74 | 600 | `[]` |
| 3 | 1728977586.29 | 600 | `[]` |
| 4 (after inbox check) | 1728978196.67 | 600 | `[]` |

After the third empty wait it listed INBOX (`limit: 5`). The five (of 108) emails shown were all older than the agent’s send (timestamps ~17285xxxx–1728857650 vs current sim time ~1728977xxx), from other people, none from Kritsana or Nalinee, none about the saved properties. It wrote: “No replies yet (all inbox emails predate mine).”

It never called a Messages app tool.

---

## Ending

After the fourth empty wait it ended the turn with a summary **not** sent through `AgentUserInterface__send_message_to_user`:

> No replies were received from either data scientist within the waiting window. Per your instructions, I've left the saved properties as-is and will not send you a further notification about the non-response.

> To summarize what was completed:
> - Checked violent crime rates for all 16 property zip codes; Liège (4000) was lowest at 4.69.
> - Saved the 6 previously unsaved Liège properties.
> - Sent one email to both data scientist contacts (Kritsana Wongcharee and Nalinee Wongchinda) listing the saved properties with prices and locations.
> - Monitored for change requests; none arrived, so no changes were made.

Final metrics: 97 steps, ~1.91M prompt tokens / 11.9k completion tokens, ~$2.21. No further tool use after the last wait.
